body.statement:
Suppose \(1<s\le2\), \(P\in\mathcal P_n\), and use
\((\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}},\mathsf F_{\mathrm{prof}})\) from
\(\mathrm{def:profile\mbox{-}cutoff\mbox{-}center}\), with
\(H=(\kappa_n/(2^{12}M))^{1/s}\) and \(\delta=\kappa_n/32\).
Establish explicit constants \(A_{\mathrm{prof}},a_{\mathrm{prof}},
C_{\mathrm{prof}}>0\), depending only on \(s,M\), such that whenever
\(T_n\ge C_{\mathrm{prof}}\log(e/\kappa_n)\), the profile-fallback
probability is controlled and, for every \(16/n\le u\le H\),
\[
 P\{\mathsf F_{\mathrm{prof}}=1\}
 +P\bigl(\{|\widehat c_{\mathrm{prof}}-c_P|>u\}
          \cap\{\mathsf F_{\mathrm{prof}}=0\}\bigr)
 \le A_{\mathrm{prof}}
       \exp\{-a_{\mathrm{prof}}m\kappa_n^2u\}.
\]
The proof must derive the population excess-risk separation for the
cross-fitted common-versus-piecewise affine profile and then derive the
sequential maximal inequality with the displayed constants; it may not
impose cross-side derivative matching.
body.justification: This lemma isolates the exact remaining higher-smoothness maximal-inequality task after the Gram and stopped Bernstein calculations.
body.gap: A uniform excess-risk gap for random cross-fitted profile scores is not yet derived under separate one-sided smoothness.
body.consumer: Closing it would certify the profile center used by the higher-smoothness interval.

obligation.what_is_open: A uniform deterministic excess-risk separation for the cross-fitted common-versus-piecewise affine profile, and its conversion into a cutoff tail with fully evaluated constants.
obligation.obstruction: The exact Gram lower bound controls coefficient stability, and the stopped Bernstein calculation controls a fixed sequential process, but the profiled quadratic score contains fitted common and piecewise coefficients.  A uniform comparison of those random fitted scores to one population profile, with no cross-side derivative matching, is still needed before the sequential bound can be applied.  Consequently the formerly asserted constants \(2^{-28}\) and \(2^{-30}\) are not justified.
obligation.attempted: The unit-flank Gram was recomputed exactly as \(H(4-\sqrt{13})/6\), the half-eigenvalue fallback was made explicit, \(H\) was retained, \(\delta\) was changed everywhere to \(\kappa_n/32\), and the exponential-series argument was carried through to the stopped sequential Bernstein formula.  Substitution into the desired profile inequalities was stopped where the missing population-to-empirical profile comparison is required.
obligation.partial_result:
Two ingredients are exact.  For either normalized unit flank,
uniformity of \(X\) gives
\[
 G_H=\int_0^H
 \begin{pmatrix}1\\x/H\end{pmatrix}
 \begin{pmatrix}1&x/H\end{pmatrix}dx
 =H\begin{pmatrix}1&1/2\\1/2&1/3\end{pmatrix},
 \qquad
 \lambda_{\min}(G_H)=\frac{H(4-\sqrt{13})}{6}.
\]
Thus the correct half-eigenvalue threshold is
\(H(4-\sqrt{13})/12\), not \(H/12\), and every approximation event
must use \(\delta=\kappa_n/32\).  Also, if
\((\xi_k,\mathcal F_k)\) are centered increments with
\(|\xi_k|\le B\), and
\(V_j=\sum_{k\le j}E(\xi_k^2\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})\), then the
exponential-series inequality gives, for \(0<\eta B<3\),
\[
 E\left[\exp\left\{\eta\xi_k-
 \frac{\eta^2E(\xi_k^2\mid\mathcal F_{k-1})}
 {2(1-\eta B/3)}\right\}\middle|\mathcal F_{k-1}\right]\le1.
\]
Multiplication and stopping at the first crossing prove the sequential
Bernstein inequality
\[
 P\left\{\max_{j\le N}\sum_{k\le j}\xi_k\ge x,
                 \ V_N\le V\right\}
 \le\exp\left\{-\eta x+
 \frac{\eta^2V}{2(1-\eta B/3)}\right\}.
\]
These calculations identify the exact Gram and stochastic constants.
They do not by themselves supply the missing uniform deterministic
lower gap for the cross-fitted quadratic profile, so no numerical
versions of the proposed downstream bounds are asserted.
